issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 06/08/26

✅ Implementation: Create Shares Table

Migration

Added migrations/20260806_create_shares.sql:

CREATE TABLE shares (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    user_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    post_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES posts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    CONSTRAINT shares_user_post_key UNIQUE (user_id, post_id)
);

CREATE INDEX idx_shares_post_id ON shares(post_id);

Model

Added Models.Share, mapped to shares, with UUID ID, user and post ownership, timestamps, relations, and the composite unique index metadata.

Constraints

  • Duplicate user-post shares are rejected at database level.
  • User deletion cascades to shares.
  • Post deletion cascades to shares.
  • The post index supports COUNT(*) WHERE post_id = ?.
  • No platform or destination data is stored.

Verification

go test ./...
go vet ./...
git diff --check

Scope

  • Create shares with a UUID primary key.
  • Associate each row with one user and one post.
  • Enforce one row per (user_id, post_id) pair.
  • Cascade-delete share rows when the associated user or post is deleted.
  • Add an index for post share-count queries.
  • Add the corresponding GORM model.

DDL

CREATE TABLE shares (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    user_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    post_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES posts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    CONSTRAINT shares_user_post_key UNIQUE (user_id, post_id)
);

CREATE INDEX idx_shares_post_id ON shares(post_id);

RESULT 06/08/26

✅ Implementation: API Share

Route

POST /posts/share
Authorization: <JWT token>
Content-Type: application/json

Payload

{
  "sid": "post-slug"
}

Changes

  • Added InsertSharePost action, controller forwarding, and posts route.
  • Restricted the endpoint to role user.
  • Resolved only published, non-private posts.
  • Inserted shares with PostgreSQL ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING.
  • Returned exist: false for a new share and exist: true for a duplicate.
  • Returned the current PostgreSQL share count.
  • Added share support to GetCounterValue and AddCounterPostV1.
  • Preserved existing post counters when updating Elasticsearch.
  • Defaulted missing counter_share fields in old Elasticsearch documents to zero.

Errors

  • 400: invalid body, missing SID, invalid user ID, or database failure.
  • 401: caller is not an authenticated user.
  • 403: post is private.
  • 409: post is missing or unpublished.
  • 500: Elasticsearch connection or update failure.

Verification

go test ./src/Utils/ElasticSearch/ElasticPost
go test ./...
go vet ./...
git diff --check

Endpoint

POST /posts/share

Scope

  • Record a share only for an authenticated user.
  • Accept the post slug through sid.
  • Count each (user_id, post_id) pair once.
  • Return HTTP 200 for duplicate requests with exist: true.
  • Return the current counter_share from PostgreSQL.
  • Reject missing, unpublished, or private posts.
  • Update counter_share in Elasticsearch only after a new row is inserted.
  • Preserve counter_comment, counter_like, and counter_view during Elasticsearch updates.
  • Do not record viewer shares or share destinations.

Request

{
  "sid": "post-slug"
}

Success Response

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": {
    "valid": true,
    "exist": false,
    "counter_share": 12,
    "messages": "Success Insert Share Post"
  }
}

RESULT 07/08/26

✅ Implementation: API Add Bookmark

Route

POST /bookmark/add
Authorization: <JWT token>
Content-Type: application/json

Changes

  • Changed existing bookmark lookup from (post_id, folder_id, user_id) to (post_id, user_id).
  • Existing bookmarks are deleted by their loaded primary key.
  • New bookmarks still use the validated folder from folder_sid.
  • Added the bookmark action to the shared post counter lookup.
  • Added counter_bookmark to the Elasticsearch post counter document.
  • Preserved all other post counters while updating bookmark totals.
  • Avoided a duplicate database count; the API response does not include the counter.

Data Flow

  1. Validate user, post, folder, visibility, and blocked-post state.
  2. Find bookmark by user and post.
  3. Insert into the selected folder or delete the existing row.
  4. Refresh the folder counter in Elasticsearch.
  5. Count rows for the post and refresh counter_bookmark in the post document.
  6. Refresh the user's Redis bookmark cache.

Verification

go test ./...
go vet ./...
git diff --check

Endpoint

POST /bookmark/add

Scope

  • Keep folder_sid validation for both supported flows: UUID when sl=true&pw=false, slug otherwise.
  • Add a published public post to the selected bookmark folder.
  • Treat bookmark state as global per (user_id, post_id), independent of folder.
  • Toggle an existing bookmark off when the same user submits the post again.
  • Keep the existing folder bookmark counter and Redis bookmark cache synchronized.
  • Count post bookmarks from PostgreSQL once after add/remove.
  • Store counter_bookmark with other post counters in Elasticsearch.
  • Preserve comment, like, view, and share counters during the update.
  • Keep the existing response contract; the counter is read through post detail.

Request

{
  "sid": "post-slug-or-id",
  "folder_sid": "folder-slug-or-id"
}

Success Response

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": {
    "valid": true,
    "messages": "Add bookmark to folder success",
    "action": "add"
  }
}

For unbookmark, action is remove.

RESULT 07/08/26

✅ Implementation: Update Bookmark Table

Migration

Added migrations/20260807_add_bookmark_user_post_unique.sql:

ALTER TABLE bookmark
    ADD CONSTRAINT bookmark_user_post_key UNIQUE (user_id, post_id);

Constraint

  • A user can bookmark a post only once.
  • folder_id remains the destination folder for a new bookmark.
  • A subsequent toggle finds the row through (user_id, post_id) and removes it.
  • Database uniqueness prevents concurrent requests from creating the same logical bookmark twice.

Existing Data

Existing duplicates must be cleaned before running the migration. Find them with:

SELECT user_id, post_id, COUNT(*) AS total
FROM bookmark
GROUP BY user_id, post_id
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;

Verification

go test ./...
go vet ./...
git diff --check

Scope

  • Enforce one bookmark row per user and post.
  • Keep folder_id to identify the selected bookmark folder.
  • Preserve existing primary key and user, post, and folder foreign keys.
  • Remove legacy duplicate (user_id, post_id) rows before applying the constraint.

DDL

ALTER TABLE bookmark
    ADD CONSTRAINT bookmark_user_post_key UNIQUE (user_id, post_id);

Pre-Migration Check

SELECT user_id, post_id, COUNT(*) AS total
FROM bookmark
GROUP BY user_id, post_id
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;

The constraint cannot be created until this query returns no rows.

issues.display_title: Issue #433:  Update View Timeline Post for Detail Post V2
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 07/08/26

✅ Implementation: Update View Timeline Post for Detail Post V2

Summary

Extended public.views_timeline_post with four fields required by Detail Post V2 while preserving every existing view-column name and position.

Columns Added

The following columns were appended after the existing hotspot column:

posts.id,
categories.name AS category_name,
posts.location_group,
posts.location_group_slug

Appending is required because PostgreSQL CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW rejects insertion before existing columns with errors such as:

ERROR: cannot change name of view column "category_id" to "id"

Category Join

Added:

LEFT JOIN panorra_dev.public.categories
    ON categories.id = posts.category_id

The LEFT JOIN preserves posts whose category relation is absent; category_name becomes NULL for those rows.

Grouping

Added these source fields to the existing GROUP BY:

categories.name,
posts.location_group,
posts.location_group_slug

posts.id was already present in the existing GROUP BY because hotspot and affiliate aggregation depend on the post identity.

Filters Preserved

No published-post filtering behavior changed:

WHERE posts.is_publish = true
  AND posts.banned = false
  AND users.banned = false

Existing calculations for potd, broadcast_data, affiliate, and hotspot remain unchanged.

Compatibility

  • View name remains public.views_timeline_post.
  • Existing columns remain in their previous order.
  • New columns exist only at the end.
  • Migration uses CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW and does not require DROP VIEW.
  • Existing dependent APIs can continue selecting the previous column set.

Files Changed

  • docs/migrations/views/DDL_views_timeline_post.sql
  • migrations/20260807_update_views_timeline_post_v2.sql

Deployment

Run the migration against the target PostgreSQL database:

migrations/20260807_update_views_timeline_post_v2.sql

Then verify:

SELECT
    id,
    category_name,
    location_group,
    location_group_slug
FROM public.views_timeline_post
LIMIT 1;

Expected result: query succeeds without dropping the view or changing existing column names.

Objective

Extend views_timeline_post with post identity, category name, and grouped-location fields required by Detail Post V2 without dropping or renaming the existing view columns.

Background

views_timeline_post is the published-post source for Timeline, Detail Post, Most Popular Posts, and other public APIs. Detail Post V2 needs fields that are not currently exposed by this view:

  • Post ID for authenticated-user like and bookmark lookups.
  • Category name instead of only category ID.
  • Location group name and slug.

PostgreSQL does not allow CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW to change existing column names or positions. All new columns must therefore be appended after the current final column, hotspot.

Requirements

  1. Preserve the name public.views_timeline_post.
  2. Use CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW; do not drop the view.
  3. Preserve every existing column name and its position.
  4. Append these fields after hotspot:
    • posts.id as id.
    • categories.name as category_name.
    • posts.location_group as location_group.
    • posts.location_group_slug as location_group_slug.
  5. Add a LEFT JOIN from posts.category_id to categories.id.
  6. Add categories.name, posts.location_group, and posts.location_group_slug to GROUP BY.
  7. Preserve the current published-post filters:
    • posts.is_publish = true.
    • posts.banned = false.
    • users.banned = false.
  8. Preserve existing potd, broadcast_data, affiliate, and hotspot behavior.

SQL Changes

Append new columns after hotspot:

COALESCE(..., '[]'::jsonb) AS hotspot,
posts.id,
categories.name AS category_name,
posts.location_group,
posts.location_group_slug

Add category join:

LEFT JOIN panorra_dev.public.categories
    ON categories.id = posts.category_id

Keep filters unchanged:

WHERE posts.is_publish = true
  AND posts.banned = false
  AND users.banned = false

Files

  • docs/migrations/views/DDL_views_timeline_post.sql
  • migrations/20260807_update_views_timeline_post_v2.sql

Verification

Apply the SQL to PostgreSQL without dropping the existing view:

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW public.views_timeline_post AS ...;

Verify the new fields:

SELECT
    id,
    category_name,
    location_group,
    location_group_slug
FROM public.views_timeline_post
LIMIT 1;

Verify existing dependent APIs can still select their previous columns without schema errors.
